AUTHOR: Olsvik, E; Trinh, CMD; Knausgård, KM; Wiklund, A; Sordalen, TK; Kleiven, AR; Jiao, L; Goodwin, M
TITLE: Biometric Fish Classification of Temperate Species Using Convolutional Neural Network with Squeeze-and-Excitation
VENUE: ADVANCES AND TRENDS IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: FROM THEORY TO PRACTICE
SPECIES: Corkwing wrasse (Symphodus melops) male and female, pollack (Pollachius pollachius), saithe/coalfish (Pollachius virens)
DATA: Own IMR temperate dataset: GoPro nest-site videos (Austevoll 2015) + stereo-BRUV (Aust-Agder, Trøndelag); Fish4Knowledge used for pre-training only
V_EV: Sec. 2.1: 'GoPro Hero4+ (black) cameras were deployed at 2-5 meters of depth'; 'cameras were deployed between 8 and 35 meters'; visibility only described qualitatively.
D_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'the applicable data set was divided into 70% training images, 15% validation images and 15% testing images' (images from videos, no grouping stated)
R_EV: Sec. 3.1: post-training used 712 images, 155 for verification 'and a subset of 155 images of the same classes were reserved for testing' (same dataset)
C_EV: Sec. 2.2: 'The final layer, softmax, applies a classifier function to obtain the probability distribution for each class per input image' (accuracy only, no threshold)
E_EV: Table 3: 'Average testing accuracy over 10 runs and time per epoch on post-training' (classification accuracy only)
ARCH: CNN-SENet (custom CNN with Squeeze-and-Excitation); compared Inception-V3, ResNet-50, Inception-ResNet-V2
METR: Accuracy, confusion matrix, time per epoch
NOTE: Text is arXiv v1; metadata venue is the IEA/AIE 2019 Springer proceedings. Classification of crops/images from field video. Headline field result: 83.68% (87.74% with augmentation) on 4-class temperate set after pre-training on Fish4Knowledge (99.27%). Split unit not stated; images drawn from videos and some S. melops individuals 'tracked and captured by camera multiple times' -> potential leakage not discussed. V3 coded NR: only 'Recording conditions varied ... especially in sun exposure' (qualitative). NIMG = 712+155+155 for the 4-class subset used.
